3.3

Return with a difference

Clarify, extend and regenerate

Systematically clarify ideas using drawing informed by established painting practice

Suggested teaching time
5–6 weeks

Timing, task steps and quantities are classroom suggestions, not NZQA grade requirements.

Read the standard (PDF)

The brief

What happens when I return to an earlier idea with a new question?

Use a related sequence of drawing and painting to clarify a personal idea, extend it and explore regeneration. Start with your own previous artwork or a new initial investigation. Treat the sequence as a thinking process, in which evaluation leads to changes in subsequent work.

Materials & preparation

Your own earlier studies, fresh observed sources where needed, drawing and painting materials selected for the inquiry, and a way to record the sequence and decisions.

Use your own drawings and photographs as starting points. Record sources and seek permission for people, places and culturally significant material. Discuss tikanga and context with your teacher where relevant.

Artist connections

Choose the connections that serve your intention. The contemporary models offer different approaches; select a relevant comparison rather than studying every artist. These works are references, not assessment exemplars.

Use the models to investigate revisiting, re-forming and revealing earlier decisions. Make a new direction grow from your own previous work and evaluate what changed.

  • Shane Cotton

    Contemporary Māori · Aotearoa New Zealand

    Cotton reworks historical references to investigate bicultural identity and colonisation. Compare how recurring forms change meaning through placement, scale and surrounding space, while keeping their particular cultural histories in view.

    Gow Langsford · artist profile and paintings · Painting investigation

  • Séraphine Pick

    Contemporary · Aotearoa New Zealand

    Pick’s atmospheric painting investigates memory, the body and states of consciousness. Compare how layered figures, shifts in colour and uncertain spaces can connect an external scene with an internal experience.

    The Arts Foundation Te Tumu Toi · artist profile · Painting investigation

  • Mark Bradford

    Contemporary · United States

    Bradford’s building-up and removal of paper connects material process with the social life of a city. Read his account of collage and décollage, then ask how adding and removing can each generate an idea.

    Art21 · artist interview on process and materials · Painting investigation

  • Frances Hodgkins

    Aotearoa New Zealand / Britain

    Look at how still-life objects and landscape can share a painted space. Try shifting the relationship between an object, its surroundings and its colour.

    Christchurch Art Gallery · Still Life

Studio sequence

Use this as a flexible route through the learning. Let the work suggest the next move.

  1. Locate a live problem

    Review your own work and identify an unresolved pictorial or conceptual issue. Choose established painting practices that can help you investigate it. Frame a question that can be answered through further drawing.

  2. Clarify in sequence

    Make related drawings that analyse and adjust the issue. Use each result to decide the next step. Keep the relationship between the works legible.

  3. Critically extend

    Evaluate which decisions are productive and pursue an implication of them. Change the relationship between form and idea, rather than adding a new effect without a reason.

  4. Revisit and regenerate

    Return to an earlier drawing or idea. Re-form it using discoveries from later work to create a new direction. Maintain the conceptual connection while testing a different visual possibility.

  5. Trace the thinking

    Order the drawings to show progression. Identify where clarification, extension or regeneration actually happens. Retain brief evaluations, but allow the visual sequence to carry the main evidence.

A useful studio conversation

Put two related works side by side. Describe what changed, show the evidence and explain what you will investigate next. Invite feedback, then make your own decision.

Presentation & submission

Your teacher will confirm the assessment window, support available, final evidence and local authenticity procedures. This sheet is an original teaching resource; it is not an NZQA-issued assessment. Compare NZQA’s annotated exemplars.

What changes between grades?

Student-friendly guidance adapted from the standard. The whole body of relevant evidence determines the grade; the examples below illustrate possibilities.

Grade distinctions for AS91451
GradeWhat the evidence needs to show
AchievementClarify an idea systematically through analysis, reflection and further drawing.In this task: Each connected work helps resolve or sharpen the initial issue.
MeritExtend the idea through critical evaluation and further development.In this task: The sequence pursues a new implication of an earlier discovery.
ExcellenceRegenerate through critically revisiting and reforming ideas from your own earlier work.In this task: A return produces a new direction that extends the inquiry rather than restyling an image.

Authority: NZQA AS91451 achievement criteria and explanatory notes (PDF).

Watch for

A sudden unrelated new subject is not necessarily regeneration; make the relationship to the previous idea visible.

Pause & reflect

Identify the return point. What did you know at that moment that you did not know when you made the original work?

These optional working notes belong to you. This website does not submit assessment evidence.

Notes and checkboxes can be saved in this browser. On a shared device, clear them before leaving.

Teacher notes

Planning, assessment & differentiation

Regeneration is required for Excellence here, while in 3.4 regeneration is present at every grade. Make that difference explicit. Students may use existing personal work as a starting point, but assess the new evidence against this standard. Agree and record how any evidence used across standards is judged independently.

Support and stretch

For teaching practice, reduce the number of simultaneous choices, model one material process and invite oral discussion alongside drawing. Offer vocabulary prompts and accessible media. To extend the learning, ask students to compare alternatives, justify a rejection or investigate a consequence of their own decision. Adapt assessed support to the standard’s conditions and any approved arrangements.

Before issuing the task

Set local start and finish dates, agree available materials and check the current standard, conditions and exemplars. Use school authenticity processes and your normal moderation procedures. Adjust this brief to the class and context; it has not been quality assured by NZQA.
